ko.executive_summary: SMIC and Leadtrend are capturing significant mature-node capacity share as TSMC and Samsung shift to advanced nodes, with SMIC posting 3.6x profit growth and Leadtrend achieving 182% QoQ net profit increase. BOM-critical mature-process demand is rebounding, though US equipment export restrictions are creating supply-chain friction for Chinese fabs.
key_facts: SMIC Q2 net profit up 3.6-fold; China revenue surged 22%
Leadtrend Q1 FY2026 gross margin rebounded to 33.6%; EPS NT$0.37, 182% QoQ profit growth
TSMC and Samsung shifting production away from 8-inch mature nodes
SMIC flagged US equipment supply delays impacting fab operations
Foreign clients shifting orders back to China fabs (SMIC)

implications.text: Migration of TSMC/Samsung capacity from mature (BCD) to advanced nodes opens supply availability for SMIC/Hua Hong at competitive pricing; BOM-critical PMIC supply tightness may ease regionally.

Leadtrend's margin recovery and strong earnings indicate high utilization of mature-node capacity; AI demand crowding out traditional mature-process slots, creating selective supply-stability gains for PMIC suppliers.
US equipment export restrictions limiting SMIC's capex velocity and tool replenishment; long-term mature-node fab productivity and cost competitiveness at risk if restrictions persist.
Capacity scarcity in mature nodes historically supports pricing; SMIC's record revenue and margin recovery suggest pricing hold in BOM-critical PMIC segments despite competitive redistribution.

ko.counterpoint: Leadtrend and SMIC margins may not sustain if AI demand normalizes and capacity rebalances; US equipment delays could impair SMIC's long-term process node maturity and qualification timelines for automotive-grade PMIC supply.
